intro.text: The Steel Ministry of the Final Empire, whose officials are called obligators. Its Canton of Finance acts as the empire's bank, directing its finances and moving its funds.

The Final Empire's church and bureaucracy in one. Its priests, the obligators, must witness every contract, wedding and land purchase, decide whom nobles may marry, and lead the worship of the Lord Ruler.

The Final Empire's church and bureaucracy in one. Its obligators witness every contract, wedding and land purchase and lead the Lord Ruler's religion, until he hands control of the Ministry from the Canton of Orthodoxy to the Steel Inquisitors.

description.text: The Canton of Finance works out of an imposing, blocky building in Luthadel, with a huge rose window between two red banners praising the Lord Ruler. Inside, an obligator sits at a desk at the end of a long entryway. The rooms are austere, with plain grey carpet and bare walls, except for a lavish waiting room with plush chairs and small cakes for visiting nobles.

Nothing important is valid without the Ministry: an event no obligator has witnessed, or a document none has sealed, might as well never have happened. Nobles pay the Lord Ruler for these services, much as they pay to rent skaa, and obligators even witness informal meetings between friends.
The Canton of Orthodoxy presides over the Ministry and its religious side. It's the Ministry's main bureaucratic division, and its obligators usually formalise contracts and agreements.
Obligators decide whom nobles may marry. The Lord Ruler expects more devotion from them than from nobles: they practise religious worship and must keep up a religious air.
Obligators shave their heads and have elaborate black tattoos around the eyes marking their rank and Canton. Seekers are among the Mistings the obligators recruit most keenly.

The Canton of Inquisition, run by the Steel Inquisitors, polices the empire, especially its Allomancers. Its members wear the usual eye tattoos plus a stark red line down the side of the face. According to Marsh, an Inquisitor can die of old age.

Around Luthadel the Canton of Inquisition keeps Soothing stations that dampen the emotions of everyone nearby, calming and depressing them so they won't rebel. Inquisitors also post Seekers there to find skaa Mistings.
There are thirty to forty Soothing stations in Luthadel, each with a staff of three Soothers and a Seeker, plus a Smoker to hide their Allomancy from anyone outside.
Marsh describes the making of an Inquisitor as "messy".

The Ministry bans political and historical writing that questions or opposes the Lord Ruler's reign. It has its own soldiers and torturers, and assassins who kill anyone too outspoken or too successful, and its obligators are the Lord Ruler's spies across the empire. It also keeps the Allomantic power of aluminum to itself.
The Inquisition's fortress, the Conventical of Seran, sits in a crater south of Luthadel. Among its torture chambers, one room holds Kwaan's inscription.

Administrators in the Canton of Inquisition gather and file information that might help with policing, covering skaa rebels, noble houses and the other Cantons. Its building in Urteau, which stands above a supply cache of the Lord Ruler's, is broad and imposing and, as is usual in Urteau, made of wood; it is plainer than most Ministry buildings, yet still has tapestries, metal trim, red rugs and a hearth in every room.
The Conventical's torture chambers are really Hemalurgic laboratories for discovering new creations, though few know their true purpose.

The Canton of Resource keeps the supply lines to the other Cantons, feeds the people and maintains the canals. Its national headquarters is in Luthadel. Its regional headquarters in Fadrex City, a single-storey, blocky, utilitarian building with flat walls and small windows, is the city's largest Ministry building, a way station between Luthadel and the cities to the west, which makes Prelan Aradan Yomen, who heads the Canton there, the city's top religious authority.

In secret, the Canton of Resource moves much of the Pits of Hathsin's atium. Obligators are always on duty at the Pits to take the metal from its geodes in a room made of metal, and the beads are hidden among coins in Ministry funds bound for Luthadel, since metal coins shine in the Cognitive Realm and keep Ruin from seeing where the atium goes.

items.text: The Ministry teaches that the ash and the mists were the Lord Ruler's punishment for the people's lack of faith.

Nobles, it teaches, owe their standing and their Allomancy to ancestors who stayed loyal to the Lord Ruler; the skaa, meanwhile, are punished for their ancestors' sins. Mistborn descend from the only men who backed him before his Ascension.
Skaa and nobles alike must fill their roles and obey the Lord Ruler, yet neither is asked for devotion or faith, and the skaa are taught little doctrine. Worshipping any other god is forbidden.

The Ministry holds that the Lord Ruler was a mortal man before his Ascension. It reveres him as the world's creator and saviour, the Sliver of Infinity: a piece of God, neither everywhere nor all-knowing, but a separate, physical part of a greater consciousness.

Its teachings sometimes mention the Well of Ascension. The Deepness, which it calls a dark monster, once threatened the world, until the Lord Ruler killed it and saved everyone. Little more is taught; religion is left to the Ministry.

The Ministry grew from the Hallant's mercantile bureaucracy; the Hallant were a people devoted to systems of measurement. The Lord Ruler used it in many secret ways beyond paperwork, such as finding new Allomantic metals and learning what they do and tracking down pure-breeding Terris bloodlines.

The Canton of Inquisition is founded some time during the Lord Ruler's sixth century on the throne. It suggests the Terris breeding programs to him, though the Terris were being subjugated long before; he agrees provisionally, and the programs continue for the rest of his reign.
Every year, new Ministry acolytes travel to Luthadel from a training facility in the north of the empire, and large sums of money travel with them.
Posing as a noble, Camon tries to swindle the Ministry. Vin Soothes Prelan Laird, then a High Prelan who pays Camon three thousand boxings, but he and a Steel Inquisitor then follow Camon's party.
When Kelsier tries to free prisoners in the square, he fights the Inquisitor Bendal and kills him.

The Inquisitors stand outside the Ministry's normal chain of command, ranked below the Lord Prelan, whose Canton of Orthodoxy leads it. Then Inquisitors capture Vin, and Kar proves she is a half-breed, the Lord Prelan's daughter. The Lord Ruler hands the Lord Prelan to the Inquisitors, who kill him, and puts the Canton of Inquisition in charge of the Ministry.

The Lord Ruler formally hands the Ministry to the Inquisitors, led by Kar. But Marsh has already killed the other Inquisitors in their sleep by pulling out their linchpin spikes, and he kills Kar the same way.
Inquisitors and high-ranking obligators take refuge at the Conventical of Seran.

King Elend Venture uses Ministry buildings for his government. The Luthadel Assembly meets in a low-ceilinged, lecture-hall-like room in the Canton of Finance's headquarters, which he has remodelled so that ordinary people can come and watch.

Elend lets obligators keep preaching, but outlaws stirring up rebellion or violence. Nearly all refuse to lend their skills to his kingdom, and Vin would rather see them out of the city. Noorden is a rare exception who often helps Elend, partly for his unusual point of view.
Straff Venture has obligators run and organise his lands.
When the Citizen takes Urteau, he doesn't burn or loot the Ministry's buildings as he does nobles' homes, but has them boarded up.

When Lord Cett leaves for Luthadel, Prelan Aradan Yomen, the highest-ranking obligator around Fadrex City, takes over, and the people, used to obligators in charge, quickly accept him. He keeps the city running in the Lord Ruler's way, still throwing balls, governs from his Canton of Resource building, feeds the people from the supply cache under the city and turns another Ministry building into an infirmary.
Buildings with stained-glass windows and long flights of steps are described as "Cantonesque".
